text:
Bungie Is 'Absolutely Not Done With Destiny,' Teases More Content - IGN Daily Fix
In today's Daily Fix:
Bungie dropped a surprise video expressing their thanks to fans for being honest about the future of Destiny. Earlier this year, Bungie made the decision to stop content development for Destiny 2, effectively ending new updates the game after nearly 10 years. But according to Bungie, they're not done yet, and promise they have more stories to tell in that universe. Bungie is also teasing the return of old content removed from Destiny 2. In other news, Final Fantasy 7 Revelation can be a very long game—about 100 hours—if you try and do _everything_. And finally, Zach Creggers adaptation of Resident Evil had a scary good debut weekend.

Street Fighter - Official 'Iconic Movement' Featurette
Don't miss 'Iconic Movement' Featurette for Street Fighter, the upcoming action-fighting movie based on the hit video game series distributed by Paramount Pictures. Take a look at the legendary moves that first debuted in the game now being translated to the live-action rendition of Street Fighter, in theaters on October 16.

Set in 1993, estranged Street Fighters Ryu and Ken Masters are thrown back into combat when the mysterious Chun-Li recruits them for the next World Warrior Tournament: a brutal clash of fists, fate, and fury. But behind this battle royale lies a deadly conspiracy that forces them to face off against each other and the demons of their past. And if they don’t, it’s GAME OVER!

Street Fighter stars Noah Centineo, Andrew Koji, Callina Liang, Joe “Roman Reigns” Anoai, David Dastmalchian, Cody Rhodes, Andrew Schulz, Orville Peck, Curtis "50 Cent" Jackson, Jason Momoa, and more. The film is directed by Kitao Sakurai and produced by Mary Parent, Cale Boyter, Jason Momoa, Takayuki Nakayama, and Stefan Makhoul.

Street Fighter is in theaters on October 16.

author: IGN YouTube
text:
Silent Hill: Townfall Review
Silent Hill: Townfall reviewed by Tristan Ogilvie on PlayStation 5. Also available on PC.

"Off the back of the more action-oriented sidestep of 2025’s Silent Hill f, Silent Hill: Townfall feels like Konami’s seminal survival horror series returning to what it does best. Its atmosphere is oppressively ominous, its central mystery is genuinely compelling to unravel and packed with themes that feel fresh, and its army of disfigured demons are exhilarating to both encounter and evade. The CRTV device that spots enemies hidden in your surroundings might slightly diminish the story’s ability to deliver major scares early on, but when Townfall eventually got me, it made sure it got me good. It also has some of the most cleverly designed and challenging puzzles I’ve experienced in any horror game in recent memory, many involving impeccable recreations of technology from yesteryear that really transported me back to its mid-nineties setting. Like the intravenous needle permanently jutting out of its hero’s wrist, Silent Hill: Townfall gives this long running series a welcome shot in the arm."
